title: Double Negation Boolean Flags (`not_` / `disable_`)
pattern: A boolean variable or function name containing a negative term (`not`, `no`, `non`, `disable`, `invalid`), especially when used in negation expressions (`!`).
why_bad: Double negatives (`!not_ready` or `!disabled`) require high cognitive load to parse, are extremely prone to logical inversion errors, and obscure the positive state of the system.
detection: Match boolean variables or functions prefixed with negative words or containing negatives when combined with logical NOT operators.
source: *The Art of Readable Code* by Dustin Boswell and Trevor Foucher (Chapter 3, p. 26); *Code Complete* by Steve McConnell (p. 607).
